title: Derived internal Hom of constructible degree-zero sheaves
statement: Let k be a field, X a separated finite-type k-scheme, ell a natural number, and Λ an ell-adic finiteness coefficient (finite normed Q_ell extension, its integral valuation ring or closed unit ball, or the finite-stage condensed algebraic closure) as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Assume ringChar(k) ≠ ell. For constructible Λ_X-module objects F,G in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], RHom(F[0],G[0]) in the ambient derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is bounded and has constructible homology [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. This includes characteristic zero; no positive-characteristic assumption is added.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, using the integral criterion of Proposition 6.6.11, Proposition 6.8.11(3) and rationalization Proposition 6.8.14.

proof.text:
The coefficient certificate includes primality of $\ell$. For an abstract finite normed extension or its closed unit ball, use the realization lemma to obtain an embedded coefficient and an exact equivalence $J$, preserving and reflecting bounded constructibility. Extension along a ring isomorphism is inverse restriction along that isomorphism, hence exact on every scheme. The scalar tensor comparison therefore gives $J(M\otimes^LN)\cong JM\otimes^LJN$. For every test object $T$, the closed adjunction gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,J\,R\mathcal Hom(K,L))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(J^{-1}T\otimes^LK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes^LJK,JL).$$
Thus the transported Hom represents the defining right adjoint for the embedded coefficient. It suffices to treat embedded integral and rational coefficients and the finite-stage algebraic closure.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15: coefficient normalization; the displayed right-adjoint argument is the explicit transport of the closed structure.

proof.text:
The spectrum of a field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. The finite-type Noetherian theorem and the dimension theorem imply that $X$ is Noetherian and finite-dimensional. Since $\ell$ is prime and $\operatorname{char}k\ne\ell$, its image in $k$ is nonzero and has an inverse; the same inverse maps to every local ring of $X$. This also applies when $\operatorname{char}k=0$.
For integral coefficients put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $B=p_X^*\underline R$. The coefficient-limit identification is an isomorphism $B\cong\widehat R_X=\varprojlim_n(R/\varpi^n)_X$, not a completion functor on input objects. For any bounded constructible integral complexes $K,L$ (not only degree-zero inputs), condition (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of the constructibility/completion bridge places these same objects in the derived-complete integral constructible category. Section-action identifies internal module objects with ordinary modules, retaining their underlying sheaves and finite presentation matrices.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1, Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3): conversion to complete constructible integral objects, with coefficient and module presentations made explicit.

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary-field adic closed-constructibility theorem to the images $P,Q$ of $K,L$ from step 2. Its hypotheses are precisely a field, invertibility of $\ell$, and separated finite type; it imposes no positive-characteristic restriction. It gives $H_R(P,Q)$ in that same complete constructible category. The module-object/ringed-site Hom comparison identifies this object with the image of the ambient relative $R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L)$, including its evaluation. Apply (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) of the bridge to this Hom object. It is bounded constructible in the general ring-object sense. This proves the integral assertion for all bounded constructible inputs, including torsion, and can therefore be used on the integral representatives in the next step.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); the existing arbitrary-field theorem supplies integral completeness and finite residue finiteness.

proof.text: For bounded constructible $E_X$-complexes $K,L$, rationalization gives bounded constructible integral representatives $K_0,L_0$ and isomorphisms $(K_0)_E\cong K$, $(L_0)_E\cong L$. The inversion theorem applies: $K_0$ is bounded constructible and $L_0$ is bounded below. Its canonical comparison identifies $R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K,L)$ with the scalar extension of $R\mathcal Hom_{B}(K_0,L_0)$. Step 3 proves that the latter integral Hom is bounded constructible, and integral-to-rational extension preserves this condition. Thus the rational assertion also holds for arbitrary bounded constructible inputs, regardless of the degrees of the chosen integral representatives.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2): integral representatives followed by internal-sheaf coefficient inversion.

proof.text: For the finite-stage algebraic-closure coefficient, predicate comparison on the Noetherian $X$ puts the given inputs in the finite constant local-model category. Since the underlying space of $X$ is Noetherian (step 2), the object-descent property (Obj) of the constructible cocone writes each as $T_{F,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ of a bounded constructible complex over some finite extension $F$; this property assumes no characteristic of $k$. Extend both to their compositum using finite-extension preservation, obtaining $K_E,L_E$ over one finite $E$ with their extensions isomorphic to the original inputs. Predicate comparison identifies their finite-model and general-lfp constructibility. In particular the finite-model hypothesis on $K_E$ in internal-Hom continuity holds. That theorem proves exactly the continuity property for all small filtered diagrams with a common termwise lower bound required by the closure Hom comparison. Since $L_E$ is bounded below, that comparison identifies the closure Hom with scalar extension of $R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K_E,L_E)$. This finite-stage Hom is bounded constructible by step 4. Extension to the closure preserves bounded constructibility; predicate comparison returns the general-lfp conclusion. Taking $K=F[0]$ and $L=G[0]$ in the relevant coefficient case proves the statement.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15: common finite-stage descent, explicit continuity hypothesis, and scalar extension.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.7.13, Definition 6.5.1, Propositions 6.6.11, 6.8.11(3), 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; assembly using existing comparison nodes.

lean.statement:
theorem boundedConstructible_hom_single
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj Λ]
    [IsCommMonObj Λ] {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom]
    [QuasiCompact X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom]
    {ℓ : ℕ} [IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient ℓ Λ] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)]
    (F G : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X.left) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ X.left))
    (hF : IsConstructibleModuleObject (condensedRingObj Λ X.left) F)
    (hG : IsConstructibleModuleObject (condensedRingObj Λ X.left) G) :
    boundedConstructible (condensedRingObj Λ X.left)
      (((derivedHom Λ X.left).obj (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj G))

split_report.summary: Repaired the positive-characteristic-only citation without changing the statement. Reused the existing arbitrary-field complete integral Hom theorem and the general-lfp/completion bridge, with dimension and module-Hom comparisons explicit. Integral and rational intermediate assertions cover bounded complexes, so descent representatives need not be degree-zero. No new nodes. All citations quoted in citations.json and all current Mathlib searches recorded from msearch.py.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves.proof.md: integral paragraph via the same complete/residue argument already stated in lem-per-adic-closed-constructible; final paragraph via inverting ell and finite-stage descent. The degree-zero item is the terminal specialization. No unit or chapter route changed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-7071fa3a7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 5 steps and every cited statement, and checked the sources in the local Bhatt–Scholze PDF: Lemma 6.7.13 (any quasi-excellent ℓ-coprime X, so finite type over any field), Prop 6.6.11, 6.8.11(3), 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15. The statement is not weakened. No new nodes. One fault (C/E hypothesis mismatch), fixed. Step 5 cited sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit, but that node is stated for a 'standing scheme' and has stmt_dep sk-def-sfb-dc-setting (char k = p > 0), so it does not apply in the characteristic-zero case the item explicitly includes. Fix: step 5 now uses (Obj) of lem-sfb-constructible-cocone-obj, a node of the same unit that holds for any X with Noetherian underlying space (supplied by step 2). proof_deps changed to match, and the sk-thm tool_use entry was removed. The other citations assume only a Noetherian scheme, an arbitrary scheme or an arbitrary field: the realization and tensor comparison, the Noetherian and dimension lemmas, the coefficient-limit identification, the bridge (i)⇔(ii)⇔(iii), the module-object Hom comparison, the rationalization equivalence, the Hom inversion (needs K₀ bounded constructible and L₀ bounded below), the extend-scalars nodes, predicate comparison, internal-Hom continuity (gives exactly the filtered-colimit hypothesis with a common lower bound) and the Q̄_ℓ Hom comparison. Step 1's Yoneda transport is correct. Edge cases checked: X empty, zero inputs, k=Q with ℓ=2, torsion integral inputs, and descent representatives not in degree zero. Batch-5 check: with this edge removed, lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence (via det-sf-flat-model-generation) is already in the target closure. It is general pro-étale stalk calculus, not part of what the trace formula or Poincaré duality state or of their proofs. The edge adds only lem-per-adic-closed-constructible and lem-per-finite-tor-internal-hom-any-field, which are integral and finite internal-Hom finiteness and are not given by either assumption: accepted. Artin–Gabber route check: lem-per-adic-closed-constructible is a Q05 child of the dropped Q144 route and is on the 10-19 drop list. The human's lock covers only artin-gabber and its three children, and this sfb item is outside them. Neither revived node uses Q̄_ℓ duality or biduality, the middle t-structure, Gabber finiteness, uniformization, alterations or stable reduction. Their proofs go through finite dévissage, thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility and ringed-site perfect duality, and both passed NY stage-1 review. The delivery justifies the use at step 3: the item's char-0 clause needs an arbitrary-field Hom finiteness that no live node gives (every other candidate assumes char p, F̄_q or a separably closed field). Accepted on the merits. Maintainer note: re-admit both nodes in route-pivot-dropped.txt at merge.
